transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Ruth (Harbor Head of Security), Samir (CTO), Elena (DevOps), Jonas (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Intro + quick customer context (Harbor is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for PII workloads).
- Security questions: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS/BYOK, data residency/retention, subprocessors.
- Next steps: send SOC2, architecture diagram, schedule deeper trial/poC conversation.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everybody, thanks for carving out time. I'm Maya, AE on the account, and joining me is Ethan, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:07] Ruth Delgado: Hi Maya. Hi Ethan. Good, thanks. Ruth here. We've got Samir and Elena as well. We're mostly here to do a security posture intake — figure out if Redwood can meet bank-level controls.
[00:15] Samir Khan: Yep, quick context from my side: legacy model infra today, thinking about moving inference to a managed vendor to reduce ops. Main constraints are data residency, encryption at rest and in transit, and strict auditability.
[00:27] Ethan Cho: Great, thanks. We'll walk through our compliance stack and deployment options — hosted, dedicated, or private — and answer any technical tradeoffs. Quick question up front: are you leaning toward dedicated or private for the PII workloads, or undecided?
[00:38] Elena Park: Undecided. We want dedicated if it reduces exposure, but if private is required for regulators then we'll need details on the private control plane and how network peering works.
[00:46] Jonas Li: Also, cost is not infinite — we need ballpark pricing to compare.
[00:50] Maya Patel: Totally — we'll include pricing. For now, let's cover security posture. Ethan, can you start on SOC2/ISO and then deep dive on KMS/BYOK?
[01:00] Ethan Cho: Sure. On SOC2: Redwood has a SOC2 Type II report — we'll share the attestation after this call. We also maintain an ISO27001 summary for our control environment. Our hosted API is audited, and Dedicated customers can get an addendum for isolation notes.
[01:18] Ruth Delgado: When you say "attestation," is that the full report or a redacted version? Our procurement usually needs the full report under NDA.
[01:25] Maya Patel: We can provide the full SOC2 Type II under NDA. I'll get that to you.
[01:29] Ruth Delgado: Good. What about penetration testing frequency and third-party scans?
[01:33] Ethan Cho: We run internal pen tests quarterly and contract an external firm annually; results are available in summary. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can coordinate joint testing windows — with a process in place.
[01:44] Samir Khan: Okay. Encryption: does Redwood support customer-managed keys? BYOK with an HSM?
[01:50] Ethan Cho: Yes, BYOK is supported for Private deployments and for Dedicated via KMS integrations. We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSMs via KMIP in some cases. There is an HSM-backed option for key material — we can share the HSM integration doc.
[02:05] Elena Park: How about hosted? If we go hosted, can we use our own keys or is that only for private?
[02:11] Maya Patel: Currently, BYOK for the hosted public offering is limited — we tend to support BYOK on Dedicated or Private where we have the customer VPC and key control. Hosted customers get provider-managed encryption, and we can discuss an enterprise contract for stronger controls.
[02:25] Ruth Delgado: Data residency — can you pin compute to a region? We need EU-only for some data sets.
[02:30] Ethan Cho: Yes, region pinning is supported. For Private we can run control plane in customer region; for Dedicated we can guarantee region placement for the GPU pool. Hosted has regional endpoints as well, but enterprise contracts can include stricter SLAs.
[02:43] Jonas Li: Another question on logs: what audit logs do you retain and how are they accessible? We need full request/response redaction controls and export for e-discovery.
[02:52] Ethan Cho: We retain request metadata and operational logs. Raw request/response retention is configurable per plan — default hosted retains short-term request logs and aggregates; Dedicated/Private can be configured to retain richer logs for longer and provide export via S3 or syslog. We also support sensitive-data redaction and token-level redaction rules.
[03:11] Ruth Delgado: Do you provide immutable audit logs or exportable STORED logs for compliance? We prefer append-only where possible.
[03:19] Ethan Cho: For Dedicated/Private we can enable write-once audit trails and send them to your own storage endpoint. We'll need to discuss retention windows and chain-of-custody.
[03:29] Samir Khan: On RBAC: how granular is your role model? Can we map to SCIM groups from our IdP?
[03:36] Maya Patel: We have granular RBAC with roles for admin, deployer, auditor, and viewer. We support SSO via SAML and provisioning via SCIM for user/group sync.
[03:45] Elena Park: Does RBAC extend to model-level controls and to per-route quotas? We need separation so product teams can't access audit logs.
[03:54] Ethan Cho: Yes, RBAC is policy-driven — you can scope permissions to projects, models, and routes. Auditing of role changes is logged.
[04:03] Ruth Delgado: SSO question: do you support multiple IdPs per tenant? We run separate IdPs for cloud and contractor access.
[04:10] Ethan Cho: We can federate multiple SAML providers, yes; there are some caveats around provisioning. We'll put detailed docs in the packet.
[04:18] Jonas Li: What's the process for a security incident? Notification windows and RTOs?
[04:22] Maya Patel: Our incident response SLA is in the enterprise contract. High-severity incidents have a 1-hour notification target and a dedicated incident channel with a named support engineer. We'll share the runbook excerpt.
[04:33] Ruth Delgado: Good. How about subprocessors — do you list all subvendors and their roles? We need to confirm no overseas data processors without explicit sign-off.
[04:41] Ethan Cho: We maintain a subprocessors list; most compute is with cloud providers like AWS/GCP and some storage partners. For Private deployments, you control the compute. We'll share the subprocessor registry and redaction rules.
[04:51] Samir Khan: Retention policy — default hosted retains 30 days for request payloads and 365 days for metadata? Can that be customized?
[04:58] Ethan Cho: Defaults vary by plan. Hosted default is more conservative (shorter request retention). Dedicated/Private allow custom retention policies — S3 export, configurable deletion TTLs, and legal hold options. We'll include sample retention configurations.
[05:12] Ruth Delgado: Is data deletion provable? Our auditors ask for verifiable deletion for e.g., GDPR requests.
[05:18] Ethan Cho: We can provide deletion logs and attestations showing deletion events. For Private deployments this is straightforward since you control the storage; for hosted we provide deletion workflows and logs under the enterprise agreement.
[05:29] Jonas Li: Any concerns about KV cache or warm-starts leaking PII between requests?
[05:34] Ethan Cho: Good callout. We have strict cache key scoping and tenant isolation at runtime — KV cache is per-tenant; in Dedicated and Private we can disable shared caching and guarantee no cross-tenant K V cashing, sorry, caching. There are also explicit TTLs and scrubbers.
[05:51] Ruth Delgado: Do you support tokenization or ephemeralization of tokens at rest to reduce exposure?
[05:56] Ethan Cho: We offer tokenization patterns in the SDK and can set up a middleware layer for incoming data to redact or tokenized sensitive fields before hitting the model.
[06:06] Maya Patel: Any regulatory frameworks beyond SOC2/ISO we should call out? PCI, HIPAA?
[06:10] Samir Khan: We're not in payments, but we do handle some health-adjacent PII, so HIPAA controls are of interest, mostly administrative and access controls.
[06:18] Ethan Cho: We can support HIPAA workflows — customers typically deploy Private or Dedicated with BAA in place. We have a BAA template and additional operational controls; we'll share that.
[06:26] Ruth Delgado: For the private control plane — is it fully customer-managed or hosted by Redwood in customer's VPC?
[06:31] Ethan Cho: Two flavors. Option A: private control plane we deploy into your VPC — you manage networking and keys. Option B: private with a customer-managed control plane in your environment and Redwood agents for runtime. We'll diagram both.
[06:45] Elena Park: For option A, how do upgrades work? We need scheduled maintenance windows and the ability to test patches in a staging VPC.
[06:53] Ethan Cho: We schedule upgrades with you, provide release notes and a canary window. For Private deployments a staging control plane is recommended; we can do blue-green deploys for the control plane.
[07:05] Jonas Li: About cost: can you show rough numbers for Dedicated GPU pool vs Private on-prem for a 100k qps-month workload?
[07:13] Maya Patel: We'll include a back-of-envelope in the follow-up, but quick answer is Dedicated tends to be cheaper than full private on-prem because of shared orchestration; we'll run numbers and show tradeoffs.
[07:24] Ruth Delgado: We also want to understand data flow mapping — where data hits, when it's logged, and where keys live.
[07:31] Ethan Cho: We'll send a detailed data flow diagram. For hosted, keys are provider-managed unless BYOK enabled on contract. For Dedicated we integrate with your KMS. For Private you own keys.
[07:43] Samir Khan: Any embargoes on who can run benchmarking tests? We'll want to run a load test to validate latency under PII load and confirm no leakage.
[07:50] Ethan Cho: We support customer-driven benchmarks; for hosted we coordinate so tests don't affect other tenants. For Dedicated/Private you'll have isolated capacity and can run full-scale benchmarks.
[07:59] Ruth Delgado: One more — legal wants SLA language on data residency and breach notification. Can you surface sample contract language?
[08:05] Maya Patel: Yes, legal samples and SLA excerpts will go in the packet.
[08:09] Jonas Li: Sounds good. If we move forward, first step is review of docs and then a technical deep dive/PoC with Ethan's team.
[08:16] Maya Patel: Perfect. To recap quickly — Redwood will send SOC2/ISO artifacts, subprocessors list, KMS/BYOK notes, architecture diagrams for hosted/dedicated/private, and preliminary pricing. Harbor will send compliance artifact list and retention requirements. We'll schedule the deep-dive for the week of Sep 8. Any final questions?
[08:30] Ruth Delgado: No more from me. Appreciate the thoroughness.
[08:34] Samir Khan: Thanks.
[08:36] Elena Park: Thanks all.
[08:38] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Friday with the doc packet.

End of meeting.
